手机远程使用电脑上的 DeepSeek Harness（dsh）：跨网点对点直连、不用架服务器；Android 还能把 dsh 跑在手机本地。"},{"id":"p8s1","text":"DSH Tether carries the DeepSeek Harness web interface to your phone over a direct peer-to-peer conne"},{"id":"p8s2","text":"ction. The agent keeps running on the machine your code lives on, and the phone gets DSH's own full "},{"id":"p8s3","text":"interface — conversations, tool calls, approvals and settings, not a reimplementation of them. Pair "},{"id":"p8s4","text":"once with a 6-digit code; after that the two ends find each other whatever network they are on."},{"id":"p9s1","text":"When there is no machine around, the same app can run DSH on the phone itself (Android) — see Local "},{"id":"p9s2","text":"there is no machine around, the same app can run DSH on the phone itself (Android) — see Local mode."},{"id":"p10s1","text":"## Features"},{"id":"p11s1","text":"Direct across networks
The two ends hole-punch to each other through iroh, and once connected nothin"},{"id":"p11s2","text":"g passes through a third party. Phone on 4G/5G and machine on home broadband works — no public IP, n"},{"id":"p11s3","text":"o tunnel service, no relay of your own. Only a failed hole-punch falls back to a relay, which carrie"},{"id":"p11s4","text":"s ciphertext it cannot read."},{"id":"p12s1","text":"DSH's own interface
What runs on your phone is DSH's own web interface, not a reimplementation: conv"},{"id":"p12s2","text":"ersations, tool calls, approvals and settings are all there. Narrow screens get adjustments — the si"},{"id":"p12s3","text":"debar becomes an overlay drawer, the settings dialog puts its navigation on top, and content takes t"},{"id":"p12s4","text":"an overlay drawer, the settings dialog puts its navigation on top, and content takes the full width."},{"id":"p13s1","text":"Several machines
My computers, at the bottom of the phone's sidebar, keeps every machine you have pa"},{"id":"p13s2","text":"ired: switch, rename, remove, or add another. Changing machines never means re-entering credentials,"},{"id":"p13s3","text":" and Connect phone on the computer mints a fresh code any time."},{"id":"p14s1","text":"Approval notifications
When the agent is waiting on your approval, the phone raises a system notific"},{"id":"p14s2","text":"ation. You approve inside DSH's own interface — this plugin deliberately does not answer approvals f"},{"id":"p14s3","text":"or you; it only carries "it's waiting for you" to your lock screen."},{"id":"p15s1","text":"## Security"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"- Pairing is a 6-digit CSPRNG code, valid 10 minutes, 3 attempts per window. After pairing, access i"},{"id":"p16s2","text":"s granted by the phone's iroh public key, which iroh's TLS verifies and nobody can forge.
- An unpai"},{"id":"p16s3","text":"red peer cannot reach your interface: proxy streams are only served on a connection that already com"},{"id":"p16s4","text":"pleted the control-stream handshake, and an unpaired connection may send at most 512 bytes before be"},{"id":"p16s5","text":"ing rejected.
- Traffic is end-to-end encrypted by iroh (QUIC/TLS). When hole-punching succeeds it t"},{"id":"p16s6","text":"ouches no third party; when it falls back, the relay only carries ciphertext it cannot read.
- The p"},{"id":"p16s7","text":"lugin's own two HTTP routes apply the same browser-trust rules dsh applies to `/api`: the `Host` mus"},{"id":"p16s8","text":"t be a loopback authority, an explicit cross-site marker is refused, and an attached `Origin` must m"},{"id":"p16s9","text":"atch the Host. Cross-site requests from a malicious page and DNS-rebinding attempts both get a 403.
"},{"id":"p16s10","text":"- **Known limit**: those rules stop a browser from being used as a confused deputy; they do **not** "},{"id":"p16s11","text":"stop a local process. A local process presents a loopback `Host`, so it can mint a pairing code and "},{"id":"p16s12","text":"pair itself as a "phone" — meaning **an attacker who can already run code on your dev machine can tu"},{"id":"p16s13","text":"rn that into long-term access**. Don't run this plugin on a machine where you run untrusted code.
- "},{"id":"p16s14","text":"**The phone side has a limit too**: the local proxy the app starts listens on 127.0.0.1 only, but an"},{"id":"p16s15","text":"y other app on the phone can connect to it and gets the full dsh interface; the port is derived from"},{"id":"p16s16","text":" the host, so it is easier to find than a random one. Untrusted apps on the phone, or an unlocked ph"},{"id":"p16s17","text":"one in someone else's hands, amount to exposing the dev machine."},{"id":"p17s1","text":"## Known limitations"},{"id":"p18s1","text":"- The iOS build is beta: built only in CI, never run on a real device, and you sign it yourself. And"},{"id":"p18s2","text":"roid is the one verified on real hardware.
- The app connects when you open it and holds no backgrou"},{"id":"p18s3","text":"nd connection — Android's doze would not let it anyway.
- The interface on the phone is DSH's own; t"},{"id":"p18s4","text":"he narrow-screen fit comes from minimal injected styles, so a dsh layout change may need a follow-up"},{"id":"p18s5","text":" here.
- English and Chinese: the app follows your phone's system language, terminal output follows "},{"id":"p18s6","text":"the computer's, and the part injected into the dsh interface follows dsh's own language setting. The"},{"id":"p18s7","text":"re is no separate language switch.
- Local mode exists only in the `arm64` build, never on iOS; the "},{"id":"p18s8","text":"phone lacks bash and a full coreutils, so shell-dependent tools are incomplete. The `arm64` APK is a"},{"id":"p18s9","text":"bout 83 MB because of the bundled runtime; the others are about 32 MB.
- Verified against dsh **`0.1"},{"id":"p18s10","text":".0-rc.7`**, **`0.1.0-rc.8`**, **`0.1.2`** (alpha and rc.1), **`0.1.5-alpha.1`**, **`0.1.5-rc.2`**, *"},{"id":"p18s11","text":"*`0.1.6-alpha.2`**, **`0.1.7-rc.2`**, **`0.2.0-rc.2`**, **`0.2.1-alpha.1`**, **`0.2.1-alpha.2`**, **"},{"id":"p18s12","text":"`0.2.1-rc.2`**, **`0.2.1-rc.3`**, **`0.2.1-rc.5`** and **`0.2.2-alpha.2`**. dsh is in developer prev"},{"id":"p18s13","text":"iew — check this line before assuming a newer dsh works. From 0.1.7 dsh refuses to install a plugin "},{"id":"p18s14","text":"whose declared range does not cover it, so a version outside this line is a refusal at install time "},{"id":"p18s15","text":"rather than a silent risk. The browser authentication dsh introduced in 0.1.2-alpha is handled entir"},{"id":"p18s16","text":"ely on the machine side; the phone app needs no update for it."}],"truncated":true}
